basis: Vascular malformations with defining skin telangiectasia and recurrent nasal bleeding; GI telangiectasia 60%, melena 30%; hepatic malformations often lack functional damage.
Inherited platelet production and function disorder with macrothrombocytopenia; bleeding does not establish separate organ damage.
Short ribs, narrow thorax and polydactyly define skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia with respiratory impairment is common (>30%); renal disease varies by subtype.
Defining aminoaciduria/acidosis, muscular dystrophy and osteoporosis indicate tubular, metabolic and skeletal disease; intellectual disability is a defining neurologic feature.
Benign squamous epithelial tumor commonly arising in oral/esophageal or nasopharyngeal/laryngeal mucosa; genital sites have no axis; skin and bladder are site-specific subtypes.
HHV8-associated vascular endothelial neoplasm, usually involving skin; visceral damage is not consistently present in at least 30%.
Bilateral congenital absence or hypoplasia of the femora; a structural skeletal disorder.
TAP2 antigen-processing immunodeficiency causes defining chronic skin ulcers; bronchiectatic airway damage is common (>30%); the metabolic classification is misleading.
Polyp confined to the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by a chromosome 3 rearrangement; malignant myeloid cells involve blood and marrow.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; neurologic impairment and muscle weakness occur in >=50%, ragged-red fibers in 2/2; hearing loss frequency unclear; ptosis is myopathic.
The defining combination is familial medullary cystic kidney disease and neurologic spastic quadriparesis.
Localized neoplasm of hematopoietic mast cells, overwhelmingly arising in skin; no systemic organ involvement is inherent.
Defined by disease of erythrocytes; infectious or other mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Lymphoid malignancy warrants hematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes; its prostate site is outside the organ axes.
Excess nutrient intake produces nutritional and metabolic imbalance; obesity and vitamin-specific organ injuries are separate subtypes or diseases.
Inherited high myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder; retinal complications remain within the ocular axis.
Glomerular disease characterized by dominant C1q-containing immune deposits and proteinuria; renal immune-mediated injury.
Inflammation of oral mucosa; the umbrella includes infectious, traumatic and treatment-related causes, so no universal immune mechanism axis.
Cancer associated with HIV infection and immunodeficiency; tumor sites and cell lineages vary, so no additional organ applies across the group.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 10/10 patients; no extra-auditory disease is defining.
Hereditary annular erythema is defined by recurrent annular skin lesions; no systemic organ damage is established.
Corneal endothelial dystrophy causes corneal clouding and reduced visual acuity in 80-99%; all defining abnormalities are ocular.
Severe developmental encephalopathy with structural brain abnormalities and defining lactic acidosis; respiratory insufficiency in 1/3 does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across 14q deletion syndromes; other organ malformations depend on the deleted interval and are not universal.
